name: Sega Dreamcast controller port (Maple Bus)
gender: female socket on the console / male plug on the controller cable
ascii:
looking into the peripheral socket (D-keyed):
    __________________________
   |                          |
   |    1      3      5        |   <- top row, 3 contacts
   |                          |
   |       2         4        |   <- bottom row, 2 contacts
   |__________________________|

   1 DATA   data/clock line (Maple), 3.3V TTL   [ref: 'Data pin 1']
   2 +5V    VCC console power (the only 5V pin)
   3 GND    ground return
   4 SENSE  tie to GND = device present
   5 DATA   data/clock line (Maple), 3.3V TTL   [ref: 'Data pin 5']
description: The proprietary 5-contact connector on a Sega Dreamcast controller cable / console port. It carries the Maple Bus: a half-duplex two-wire serial bus (SDCKA + SDCKB) that the console powers with 5 V but signals at 3.3 V TTL. The two data lines alternate clock and data roles every bit; the host runs ~2 Mbps and polls attached peripherals about every 16 ms. A 5th 'sense' contact is tied to ground to announce that a device is plugged in. Physically the two data lines are the outer pins of the top row (1 and 5); power, ground and sense fill pins 2-4.

contacts.name: SDCKA
contacts.description: Serial Data/Clock line (one of the two Maple data lines), 3.3 V TTL. Reference pinouts label this 'Data pin 1'. The two data lines swap clock/data role every bit and idle HIGH via a weak pull-up. Which physical line is SDCKA vs SDCKB is not fixed across sources, confirm by scope/continuity.

contacts.name: VCC
contacts.description: +5 V supply from the console (powers the peripheral). The only 5 V pin.

contacts.name: SENSE
contacts.description: Device-present sense. Commonly tied to GND to tell the console a peripheral is attached (the DC also detects via Maple polling, so some designs omit it).

contacts.name: SDCKB
contacts.description: Serial Data/Clock line (the other Maple data line), 3.3 V TTL. Reference pinouts label this 'Data pin 5'. Swaps clock/data role with the pin-1 line every bit and idles HIGH.

variants: The controller itself acts as a Maple host to its own sub-peripherals (VMU, Puru Puru rumble pack) over the expansion-slot 'LM bus' -- a Maple-style bus one level down.

Wire colors are NOT standardized across cables/controllers. A commonly-seen mapping is red=VCC, black=GND, white=sense, with the two remaining wires as the data lines -- but always confirm with a meter, do not trust the colors.
gotchas: Pin numbering (this entry): aligned to the RNT / dreamcast.wiki peripheral pinout -- 1=DATA, 2=+5V, 3=GND, 4=SENSE, 5=DATA. The two DATA lines are the OUTER pins of the top row (1 and 5); +5V and SENSE are the bottom pair (2 and 4). Other projects (e.g. GP2040-CE) number the same connector differently, so a pin number only means something within one source's convention -- identify each wire by continuity, never by pin number or wire color.

Data lines are 3.3 V TTL, NOT 5 V -- only VCC (pin 2) is 5 V. A 3.3 V MCU (RP2040/Pico) reads and drives the data lines directly, so NO level shifter is required. (Some older projects level-shifted out of caution; it is not needed.)
Ring out VCC and GND first, then identify the two data lines and the sense wire BEFORE soldering -- especially on a cut-off cable with bare leads.

This is not UART or SPI. The two data lines swap clock/data roles every bit and data is latched on the clock line's falling edge, so you need bit-level handling -- on an RP2040 that means a PIO program (see the Maple-bus Pico projects), not a hardware UART/SPI block.
Both data lines idle HIGH through weak pull-ups; the bus is half-duplex.
Pin 4 (sense): tie to GND to signal 'device present.' Leaving it floating can make the console fail to see the peripheral in some setups.
The console polls peripherals about every 16 ms (60 Hz) -- a device must answer within that window to register on a given frame.
notes: Pin numbering aligned to the RNT / dreamcast.wiki peripheral pinout (1=DATA, 2=+5V, 3=GND, 4=SENSE, 5=DATA) -- this CORRECTS an earlier draft that had 1=VCC/2=SDCKA/3=SDCKB/4=SENSE/5=GND. No manufacturer datasheet exists for this proprietary connector, so verified stays false; confirm wire-to-pin mapping and SDCKA-vs-SDCKB data-line identity on the bench with a meter/scope. 3.3 V-TTL data level per dreamcast.wiki and working no-level-shifter RP2040 builds (GP2040-CE, OrangeFox86 DreamcastControllerUsbPico).
